New 7-Zip Vulnerabilities Let Attackers Execute Arbitrary Code and Compromise Systems

Cyber Security News
2026-05-26 10 use cases 6 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

A critical heap buffer overflow vulnerability has been disclosed in 7-Zip version 26.00, enabling attackers to achieve arbitrary code execution via a vtable hijack by exploiting a defect in the tool&#8217;s NTFS archive handler. Tracked as CVE-2026-48095 and assigned advisory GHSL-2026-140, the flaw resides in the CInStream::GetCuSize() function inside NtfsHandler.cpp. The function computes the NTFS [&#8230;] The post New 7-Zip Vulnerabilities Let Attackers Execute Arbitrary Code and Compromise Systems appeared first on Cyber Security News .

Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] 7-Zip (7zFM.exe/7z.exe) spawning shell or LOLBin child — CVE-2026-48095 vtable hijack Exploitation High
Hunts successful exploitation of the CVE-2026-48095 NTFS-handler heap overflow, where a crafted NTFS image opened in 7-Zip hijacks the CInStream vtable and executes attacker code. 7-Zip is a pure archiver and should never spawn cmd/PowerShell/script-host/LOLBin children, so a 7zFM.exe/7z.exe/7zG.exe parent of those processes is a high-fidelity post-exploitation signal. Rationale: Anchored on the article's named binaries (7-Zip opens the file, 7zFM.exe/7z.exe) and the documented vtable-hijack→arbitrary-code-execution outcome. An archiver parenting a shell/LOLBin is near-zero in normal use, giving a sharp post-exploit signal. Cross-checked the CVE/GHSL-2026-140 details against the GitHub Security Lab advisory and two independent write-ups. Cross-checked against: • https://teamwin.in/new-7-zip-vulnerabilities-let-attackers-execute-arbitrary-code-and-compromise-systems/ • https://cybersixt.com/a/miqspHyobiMqpgot2dWbzD • https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/
ATT&CKT1203 T1204.002 T1059
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("7zFM.exe","7z.exe","7zG.exe","7zr.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith @"\7zFM.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith @"\7z.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith @"\7zG.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith @"\7zr.exe"
| where NewProcessName has_any (@"\cmd.exe",@"\powershell.exe",@"\pwsh.exe",@"\wscript.exe",@"\cscript.exe",@"\mshta.exe",@"\rundll32.exe",@"\regsvr32.exe",@"\bitsadmin.exe",@"\certutil.exe",@"\curl.exe")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Exposed endpoints running vulnerable 7-Zip ≤ 26.00 (CVE-2026-48095) Weaponization High
Identifies the initial-access exposure surface for CVE-2026-48095: any host with 7-Zip version 26.00 or earlier where merely opening a delivered crafted NTFS image (under any extension) triggers the heap overflow. The flaw exists in every build through 26.00, so this enumerates all at-risk installs for prioritised patching. Rationale: Anchored on the article's explicit affected-version statement ('All 7-Zip versions through 26.00 are affected') and CVE-2026-48095, giving a deterministic, low-FP exposure inventory. Software inventory/TVM telemetry has no Sysmon/FDR/CloudTrail equivalent, so this is Defender/Sentinel-only. Cross-checked against: • https://teamwin.in/new-7-zip-vulnerabilities-let-attackers-execute-arbitrary-code-and-compromise-systems/ • https://cybersixt.com/a/miqspHyobiMqpgot2dWbzD
ATT&CKT1203 T1204.002
Data sources
DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
| where SoftwareName has "7-zip"
| extend ParsedVer = parse_version(SoftwareVersion)
| where ParsedVer <= parse_version("26.00")   // every build through 26.00 carries the GetCuSize defect
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, EndOfSupportStatus
| order by SoftwareVersion asc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId =~ "CVE-2026-48095" or (SoftwareName has "7-zip")
| extend ParsedVer = parse_version(SoftwareVersion)
| where CveId =~ "CVE-2026-48095" or ParsedVer <= parse_version("26.00")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by DeviceName asc

title: Crypto-Wallet Keystore Access by Non-Wallet Process

status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers / wallet drainers read keystore files from MetaMask,
    Exodus, Atomic, Phantom, Bitcoin, Electrum, Ethereum-cli wallets.
    Filtering out the legitimate wallet binaries leaves only attacker
    activity.
references:

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

detection:

            - '\Exodus\'
            - '\Electrum\wallets\'
            - '\MetaMask\'
            - '\Phantom\'

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-48095")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-48095")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION

    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-48095")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] InvisibleFerret Cython module load: python interpreter loading mod/pad/brw .pyd/.so from .vscode Installation High
Hunts a Python interpreter loading Cython-compiled InvisibleFerret extension modules (mod.pyd/pad.pyd/brw.pyd on Windows, *.so on macOS) from a .vscode directory. This is the article's core evasion: the payload is a native extension module loaded by python, so script-content detections miss it but the image-load of the named .pyd from a developer .vscode path is high-fidelity. Rationale: Uses the exact module filenames (mod.pyd/pad.pyd/brw.pyd/mc.so) and the .vscode drop path named in Trend Micro's IOC table, paired with a python interpreter as the loader — a combination legitimate dev work almost never produces. Cross-checked Trend Micro and Microsoft's Contagious Interview reporting. Cross-checked against: • https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/26/e/analyzing-void-dokkaebi-invisibleferret-malware.html • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/03/11/contagious-interview-malware-delivered-through-fake-developer-job-interviews/ • https://gbhackers.com/invisibleferret-malware-uses-pyd/
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1204.002 T1027.013

| where FileName in~ ("mod.pyd","pad.pyd","brw.pyd","mod.so","pad.so","brw.so","mc.so")
| where FolderPath has ".vscode"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate

| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (".mod","mod.pyd","pad.pyd","brw.pyd","mod.so","pad.so","brw.so","mc.so","pad0","brw0","mc0")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] InvisibleFerret/BeaverTail module + loader-script drop into .vscode directory Installation High
Hunts file writes of the named Cython modules (mod/pad/brw/mc .pyd/.so) and their runtime loader scripts (.mod, pad0, brw0, mc0) into a .vscode directory. This is the staging step the actor uses to disguise compiled binaries as developer workspace files and slip past script-pattern scanning. Rationale: Anchors on the exact IOC filenames and the .vscode drop path from Trend Micro's table; the loader-script names (.mod/pad0/brw0/mc0) are unique enough that any write into .vscode is suspicious. Corroborated by Trend Micro and gbhackers. Cross-checked against: • https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/26/e/analyzing-void-dokkaebi-invisibleferret-malware.html • https://gbhackers.com/invisibleferret-malware-uses-pyd/

[LLM] InvisibleFerret C2 beacon to 45.59.160.199 and /clw/ download paths Command & Control High
Hunts outbound connections to the hardcoded InvisibleFerret C2 IP 45.59.160.199 and HTTP requests to the /clw/{sType} (Windows) and /clw1/{sType} (macOS) download paths used by the Cython mod module to pull further payloads. Targets the C2 stage regardless of how the module was loaded. Rationale: 45.59.160.199 was recovered from the Cython binary via XOR decoding and the /clw//clw1/ paths are the distinct Windows/macOS download URIs in the IOC table — both are direct, high-confidence network IOCs. Confirmed against Trend Micro's report. Cross-checked against: • https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/26/e/analyzing-void-dokkaebi-invisibleferret-malware.html • https://gbhackers.com/invisibleferret-malware-uses-pyd/

| order by Timestamp desc

[LLM] InvisibleFerret/BeaverTail ip-api.com geolocation lookup from non-browser process Command & Control Medium
Hunts requests to ip-api.com/json (the external geolocation service abused by the InvisibleFerret pad module and BeaverTail njs variant for victim network fingerprinting) initiated by a non-browser process such as python or node. Browsers calling ip-api.com are normal; an interpreter doing it on a developer endpoint is the discovery signal. Rationale: ip-api.com/json is explicitly named in the IOC table as abused by BeaverTail (njs) and the pad module; restricting to python/node initiators removes the heavy browser/legit-app noise so the remaining hits are interpreter-driven host fingerprinting. Confirmed against Trend Micro's report. Sentinel DNS table lacks process attribution, so the Sentinel variant is broader — noted as Medium confidence. Cross-checked against: • https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/26/e/analyzing-void-dokkaebi-invisibleferret-malware.html • https://gbhackers.com/invisibleferret-malware-uses-pyd/
ATT&CKT1614.001 T1016 T1071.001
Data sourcesWeb
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "ip-api.com"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python","node","pythonw") or InitiatingProcessFileName endswith ".pyd"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DnsQuery has "ip-api.com"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject

     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")

                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Cloud Atlas APT Group Modifies termsrv.dll to Enable Multiple RDP Sessions on Victim Hosts

Cyber Security News
2026-05-25 21 use cases 7 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

A well-known advanced persistent threat group called Cloud Atlas has been caught using a dangerous technique to hijack Windows systems without alerting anyone on the network. The group modifies a core Windows file called termsrv.dll to unlock multiple simultaneous Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) sessions on a victim&#8217;s computer. This lets attackers work in the background [&#8230;] The post Cloud Atlas APT Group Modifies termsrv.dll to Enable Multiple RDP Sessions on Victim Hosts appeared first on Cyber Security News .

[LLM] Cloud Atlas termsrv.dll patch enabling concurrent RDP sessions (takeown/icacls/sc) Installation High
Hunts the headline Cloud Atlas technique: rdp_new.ps1 takes ownership of C:\Windows\System32\termsrv.dll, grants full rights, patches the single-session byte sequence, then restarts TermService so multiple simultaneous RDP sessions are allowed. Detects the takeown+icacls+sc-restart command sequence and the actual modification of the protected system DLL by a non-TrustedInstaller process. Rationale: Anchored on the article's exact technique chain — takeown + icacls /grant against System32\termsrv.dll followed by a TermService restart — corroborated by Securelist (cloud-atlas-2026/119895) and gbhackers. Patching a TrustedInstaller-protected system DLL from a user-context process is near-zero in clean environments. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/cloud-atlas-2026/119895/ • https://gbhackers.com/apt-group-patches-termsrv-dll/
ATT&CKT1021.001 T1562.001 T1562.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let Patchers = DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "termsrv.dll"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("takeown", "icacls", "/grant")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
let DllWrites = DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FolderPath has @"\System32\termsrv.dll" and ActionType in ("FileModified","FileCreated","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TiWorker.exe","TrustedInstaller.exe","poqexec.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, ActionType, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName;
Patchers
| join kind=inner (DllWrites) on DeviceId
| where abs(datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, Timestamp1)) <= 600
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, DllWriteAction = ActionType, DllPath = FolderPath, DllWriter = InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
let Patchers = SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where CommandLine has "termsrv.dll"
| where CommandLine has_any ("takeown", "icacls", "/grant")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project PatchTime = TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, CommandLine, NewProcessName;
let SvcRestart = SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where CommandLine has "TermService" and CommandLine has_any ("stop","start","restart","config")
| project SvcTime = TimeGenerated, Computer, SvcCmd = CommandLine;
Patchers
| join kind=inner SvcRestart on Computer
| where abs(datetime_diff('second', PatchTime, SvcTime)) <= 600
| project PatchTime, Computer, SubjectUserName, CommandLine, SvcCmd
| order by PatchTime desc

[LLM] Cloud Atlas PowerCloud / RevSocks payloads masquerading in Windows system folders Installation High
Hunts execution or drop of Cloud Atlas PowerCloud and RevSocks binaries that masquerade as system files inside unusual Windows subdirectories (e.g. C:\Windows\wininet.exe, C:\Windows\pla\reports.exe, C:\Windows\System32\timecontrolsvc\vmnetdrv64.exe, C:\ProgramData\hp\client.exe). These exact paths are reported IOCs and are not legitimate Windows locations for executables. Rationale: Uses the exact reported PowerCloud/RevSocks file paths. wininet.exe is a real DLL but never a standalone EXE in C:\Windows root; reports.exe/winlog.exe/vmnetdrv64.exe under PLA/timecontrolsvc are fabricated locations — any hit is high-fidelity regardless of file-hash polymorphism. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/cloud-atlas-2026/119895/ • https://www.technadu.com/cloud-atlas-apt-targets-russia-and-belarus-government-and-diplomatic-entities-with-powercloud-tool/628312/
ATT&CKT1036.005 T1564.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem

  @"\Windows\PLA\System\bounce.exe",
  @"\ProgramData\hp\client.exe"]);
union
( DeviceProcessEvents

( DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)

  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Event="FileDrop", Path=FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName )
| order by Timestamp desc

[LLM] Cloud Atlas reverse SSH tunnel via renamed ssh binaries to attacker C2 Command & Control High
Hunts the Cloud Atlas backup access channel: renamed OpenSSH clients (C:\Windows\PLA\System\conhosts.exe, C:\Windows\INF\BITS\esentprf.exe) initiating outbound connections — typically to port 22 or the reported SOCKS/SSH-tunnel servers — to establish reverse tunnels that bypass inbound firewall rules. Pairs the masqueraded binary with public egress for high signal. Rationale: Combines two article IOCs — the renamed ssh binaries (conhosts.exe in PLA, esentprf.exe in INF\BITS) and the reported SSH-tunnel C2 IPs — so a hit requires both a masqueraded SSH client and public egress, which is essentially never benign. Corroborated by Securelist's note that Cloud Atlas layers SSH/RevSocks tunnels. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/cloud-atlas-2026/119895/ • https://gbhackers.com/apt-group-patches-termsrv-dll/
ATT&CKT1572 T1090 T1021.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\PLA\System\conhosts.exe", @"\INF\BITS\esentprf.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("conhosts.exe","esentprf.exe")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| extend KnownC2 = (RemoteIP in (C2ips)) or (RemoteUrl has_any (C2domains))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, KnownC2
| order by Timestamp desc

| where DstIpAddr !startswith "10." and DstIpAddr !startswith "192.168." and DstIpAddr !startswith "172."
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkApplicationProtocol, DvcAction

[LLM] Cloud Atlas VBS tunnel/keep-alive scripts executed from INF and PLA directories Installation High
Hunts wscript/cscript executing the Cloud Atlas reverse-SSH tunnel VBS scripts staged in non-standard locations — C:\Windows\INF\Run.vbs, C:\Windows\INF\install.vbs, and C:\Windows\PLA\System\{Gen,Kill,Run}.vbs — which generate keys, start, and restart the SSH tunnel and are registered as scheduled tasks for persistence. Rationale: Targets the exact VBS filenames and staging directories reported (INF\Run.vbs, PLA\System\Gen.vbs/Kill.vbs/Run.vbs). C:\Windows\INF and PLA are real OS dirs but are never legitimate homes for user VBS scripts, so wscript/cscript executing these specific names is a precise IOC. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/cloud-atlas-2026/119895/
ATT&CKT1059.005 T1053.005

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\INF\Run.vbs", @"\INF\install.vbs", @"\PLA\System\Gen.vbs", @"\PLA\System\Kill.vbs", @"\PLA\System\Run.vbs")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "wscript.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "cscript.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any (@"\INF\Run.vbs", @"\INF\install.vbs", @"\PLA\System\Gen.vbs", @"\PLA\System\Kill.vbs", @"\PLA\System\Run.vbs")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Cloud Atlas C2 / SOCKS-proxy / Tor egress to reported infrastructure Command & Control Medium
Hunts host or network telemetry showing connections or DNS resolutions to the reported Cloud Atlas reverse-SSH/SOCKS-proxy domains and Tor C2 IP set. Use as an IOC-pivot detection to surface any endpoint beaconing to the campaign infrastructure, including the AWS-hosted Tor nodes (3.125.114.0/24). Rationale: Pure IOC pivot on the campaign's full reported C2 IP and domain set (SSH-tunnel, SOCKS-proxy, and Tor nodes incl. AWS 3.125.114.x). Confidence Medium because IOC sets age out; corroborated against Securelist's published infrastructure. Capturing the initiating process turns a hit into a host-attributable lead. [LLM] Cloud Atlas PowerShower persistence: PowerShell running googleearth.ps1 from Pictures Installation High
Hunts the PowerShower reconnaissance/lateral-movement loader running from its reported persistence path C:\Users\<user>\Pictures\googleearth.ps1 — PowerShell executing a .ps1 out of a user's Pictures folder, an atypical script location used to blend in with image files. Rationale: Uses the exact reported PowerShower persistence path C:\Users\<user>\Pictures\googleearth.ps1. A PowerShell script in the Pictures directory is intrinsically anomalous and the filename masquerades as a Google Earth asset, making this a clean single-event detection. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/cloud-atlas-2026/119895/ • https://securelist.com/cloud-atlas-attacks-with-new-backdoor-vbcloud/115103/
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has @"\Pictures\googleearth.ps1"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "powershell.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine has @"\Pictures\googleearth.ps1"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Cloud Atlas PowerShower googleearth.ps1 Execution from Pictures
id: c81a4d6e-2f30-4b59-9a7c-5e1d0b3f8a26
description: Detects PowerShell executing the Cloud Atlas PowerShower loader from a user's Pictures folder (googleearth.ps1).
references:
  - https://securelist.com/cloud-atlas-2026/119895/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/25
tags:
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.t1036.005
  - attack.g0100
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: '\Pictures\googleearth.ps1'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe) @CommandLine:(*\\Pictures\\googleearth.ps1* OR *\\Pictures\\GoogleEarth.ps1*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i
| CommandLine=/\\Pictures\\googleearth\.ps1/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies

ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2018-0802")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2018-0802")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard Installation High
ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.
ATT&CKT1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe")
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\atera_agent.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\SplashtopStreamer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\RustDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\NinjaOne.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Remote-Management (RMM) Tool Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0c
status: experimental
description: |
    AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera / Splashtop /
    RustDesk — RMM tools attackers commonly install for hands-on-
    keyboard access. Filter against the IT estate's known tool.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1219/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1219
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\AnyDesk.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer_Service.exe'
            - '\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe'
            - '\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe'
            - '\atera_agent.exe'
            - '\SplashtopStreamer.exe'
            - '\RustDesk.exe'
            - '\NinjaOne.exe'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - IT-approved RMM in use across the estate. Maintain a known-IT-
      tool exclusion list per environment.
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027

let BadHashes = dynamic(["1a11b26dd0261ef27a112ce8b361c247", "5329f7bff9d0d5db28821b86c26d628f", "7a95360b7e0eb5b107a3d231abbc541a", "c0d1eaa15a2cefbab9735787575c8d8e", "d5b38b252cf212a4a32763de36732d40", "3c75cedb1196df5eab91f31411ed4b33", "42ac350bfbc5b4eb0fedba16c81919c7", "493b901d1b33eb577db64aadd948f9ce", "2cabb721681455dae1b6a26709def453", "1b39e86eb772a0e40060b672b7f574f1", "1d401d6e6fc0b00aaa2c65a0ac0cfd6b", "40a562b8600f843b717bc5951b2e3c29", "2b4ba4facf8c299749771a3a4369782e", "ba9ce06641067742f2afc9691faff1dc", "fb0f8027acf1b1e47e07a63d8812ed50", "bbf1fa694122e07635deeac11ad712f8", "f301aa3d62b5095eec4d8e34201a4769", "f9c3bbe108566d1a6b070f9c5fb03160", "369b75bdcded16469ede7ab8bedcfae1", "9eaae9491f6a50d6df0be393734a44cb", "3e6e9df00a764b348ec611ee8504aca0", "9bd788f285e32a05e6591d1eb36ebffc", "f42085522ec2ebb16edcf814e7c330ad", "2042eb5d52f0b535a1ce6b6f954c8c2b", "2aa1e9765ef6b00b94a9b6be0041436a", "36120f5e9411bcbac7104ef3fa964ed2", "5000a353399500bc78381dc95b6ed2dc", "579a9952d31cad801a3988dbe7914ce7", "867b634588c0fd6b26684d502c15ab03", "38fa4306fa4406ba31cf171af4d36e34"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate

        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)

                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: File or Process Matching Article Hash IOCs
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0b
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__HASH_LIST__` placeholder with article-specific SHA256
    values. Use a watchlist or external indicator file for management
    at scale.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Hashes|contains:
            - 'SHA256=__HASH_PLACEHOLDER_REPLACE_ME__'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive hash match
level: critical

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Connection to Exillio404 money-mule .onion forum (Telegram MaaS C2 marketplace) · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] Connection to Exillio404 money-mule .onion forum (Telegram MaaS C2 marketplace) Command & Control High
Hunts any host in the estate resolving or connecting to the Exillio404 Brazilian dark-web mule forum onion address (exiliow4ctlzrvaglkgwqnpxdlvrxmdgvuy2hkbzqoziebfim6q5hwid.onion) named in KELA's Mule-as-a-Service report. A hit means a corporate or analyst host touched a known laundering-tradecraft marketplace — directly via a Tor client or indirectly via a tor2web gateway (e.g. *.onion.to / *.onion.ly). This is the only article-specific, high-fidelity IOC in the piece. Rationale: Anchored on the exact Exillio404 onion string (exiliow4ctlzrvaglkgwqnpxdlvrxmdgvuy2hkbzqoziebfim6q5hwid.onion) from the article's IOC table and code block — a literal, near-zero-FP indicator. Substring match also catches tor2web gateway forms (onion.to/onion.ly). Campaign corroborated by KELA's own report and MIT Technology Review, though the onion address itself is single-source (KELA/CSN). Cross-checked against: • https://www.kelacyber.com/blog/mule-as-a-service-money-laundering/ • https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/04/15/1135898/cyberscammers-bypassing-bank-telegram/ • https://gbhackers.com/verified-bank-mule-accounts/
ATT&CKT1090.003 T1102.002

let onion = "exiliow4ctlzrvaglkgwqnpxdlvrxmdgvuy2hkbzqoziebfim6q5hwid.onion";
union
  (DeviceNetworkEvents | where Timestamp > ago(30d) | where RemoteUrl has onion | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source="NetworkRemoteUrl", InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort),
  (DeviceProcessEvents | where Timestamp > ago(30d) | where ProcessCommandLine has onion | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source="ProcessCmdLine", InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=ProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl="", RemoteIP="", RemotePort=int(null)),
  (DeviceFileEvents | where Timestamp > ago(30d) | where FileOriginUrl has onion | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source="FileOriginUrl", InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl=FileOriginUrl, RemoteIP="", RemotePort=int(null))
| order by Timestamp desc
let onion = "exiliow4ctlzrvaglkgwqnpxdlvrxmdgvuy2hkbzqoziebfim6q5hwid.onion";
union isfuzzy=true
  (CommonSecurityLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where RequestURL has onion or DestinationHostName has onion | project TimeGenerated, Source="Proxy", SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct),
  (DnsEvents | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where Name has onion | project TimeGenerated, Source="DNS", SourceIP=ClientIP, DestinationHostName=Name, RequestURL="", DeviceVendor="", DeviceProduct=Computer),
  (W3CIISLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where csUriStem has onion or csUriQuery has onion | project TimeGenerated, Source="IIS", SourceIP=cIP, DestinationHostName=Computer, RequestURL=csUriStem, DeviceVendor="", DeviceProduct="")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process Actions on Objectives High

ATT&CKT1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Ethereum\keystore\", @"\Bitcoin\", @"\Exodus\", @"\Electrum\wallets\", @"\MetaMask\", @"\Phantom\", @"\Atomic\Local Storage\")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Ethereum\keystore\", @"\Bitcoin\",
                                  @"\Exodus\", @"\Electrum\wallets\",
                                  @"\MetaMask\", @"\Phantom\",
                                  @"\Atomic\Local Storage\")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe",
                                  "electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |

    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:

author: Clankerusecase

level: high
ENDPOINT

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem

        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process Exploitation High
