Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender · Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — ⚡ Weekly Recap: Linux Flaws, Defender 0-Days, Router Botnets, and Supply Chain C
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → Suspicious browser extension installation · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

    - attack.t1555.003

logsource:

detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'

    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator Delivery High
External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1566
Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent
  ExternalParticipants=*
| where match(SenderDisplayName, "(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)")
| stats count, earliest(_time) as firstTime, latest(_time) as lastTime
    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

FBI warns of Kali365 phishing service targeting Microsoft 365 accounts

BleepingComputer
2026-05-25 13 use cases 5 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

The FBI is warning about the Kali365 phishing-as-a-service platform (PhaaS) that is used to hijack Microsoft 365 accounts by abusing OAuth device code authentication to steal session tokens and bypass multi-factor authentication (MFA). [...]

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Microsoft 365 OAuth device code authentication flow (Kali365 token theft) · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Attacker device registration in victim Entra tenant after device-code compromise · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Microsoft 365 sign-in from Kali365 phishing infrastructure IPs · [LLM] Endpoint connection or DNS lookup to Kali365 Cookie Link AitM domains · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Kali365 post-compromise mailbox hiding rule (spam/phish/click/link/SharePoint keywords) · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] Microsoft 365 OAuth device code authentication flow (Kali365 token theft) Exploitation Medium
Hunts successful Entra/M365 sign-ins completed via the OAuth 2.0 device authorization grant, the core technique Kali365 abuses to steal session tokens and bypass MFA. Device code flow is rare in most tenants, so a sudden appearance — especially for new users or unusual client apps — is a strong account-takeover signal. Rationale: Built on Kali365's defining TTP — abuse of Microsoft's OAuth 2.0 device authorization grant (microsoft.com/devicelogin) to mint tokens without solving MFA. Arctic Wolf and the FBI PSA both center the campaign on device code flow; reprise99's Sentinel repo confirms the AuthenticationProtocol=='deviceCode' detection pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://arcticwolf.com/resources/blog/token-bingo-dont-let-your-code-be-the-winner/ • https://github.com/reprise99/Sentinel-Queries/blob/main/Azure%20Active%20Directory/Identity-DeviceCodePhishing.kql • https://www.theregister.com/cyber-crime/2026/05/22/fbi-warns-of-kali365-as-device-code-phishing-soars/5245024
ATT&CKT1566 T1528 T1078.004
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication
// Device code flow marker lives in AuthenticationProcessingDetails when the dedicated AuthenticationProtocol column is unavailable
AADSignInEventsBeta
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ErrorCode == 0
| extend ProcDetails = tostring(AuthenticationProcessingDetails)
| where ProcDetails has "Device Code"
| summarize SignInCount = count(), Apps = make_set(Application), SrcIPs = make_set(IPAddress), Countries = make_set(Country), arg_max(Timestamp, *) by AccountUpn
| project Timestamp, AccountUpn, Application, IPAddress, Country, City, DeviceTrustType, SignInCount, Apps, SrcIPs, Countries
| order by Timestamp desc
// Canonical field is AuthenticationProtocol == "deviceCode"; this tenant schema exposes AuthenticationProcessingDetails, parsed below
let Lookback = 14d;
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where ResultType == 0
| extend ProcDetails = tostring(AuthenticationProcessingDetails)
| where ProcDetails has "Device Code"
| summarize SignInCount = count(), Apps = make_set(AppDisplayName), SrcIPs = make_set(IPAddress), Locations = make_set(Location), arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by UserPrincipalName
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, AppDisplayName, IPAddress, Location, ClientAppUsed, SignInCount, Apps, SrcIPs, Locations
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Microsoft 365 OAuth Device Code Authentication Flow

CLOUD
index=azure sourcetype="azure:aad:signin" "properties.authenticationProtocol"="deviceCode" "properties.status.errorCode"=0
| stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values("properties.appDisplayName") as apps values(src_ip) as src_ips dc(src_ip) as ip_count by user

[LLM] Kali365 post-compromise mailbox hiding rule (spam/phish/click/link/SharePoint keywords) Actions on Objectives High
Hunts creation of malicious Outlook/Exchange inbox rules that auto-move and mark-as-read messages matching Kali365's documented keyword set (spam, phish, click, link, SharePoint). Arctic Wolf observed operators planting these rules immediately after device-code token theft to suppress security warnings and victim replies. Rationale: Uses Arctic Wolf's exact reported rule logic — keyword set (spam/phish/click/link/SharePoint) combined with move-to-folder + mark-as-read actions designed to hide phishing-warning and reply traffic. The keyword+action pairing makes this far more specific than a generic 'new inbox rule' alert. Cross-checked against: • https://arcticwolf.com/resources/blog/token-bingo-dont-let-your-code-be-the-winner/ • https://cyberscoop.com/fbi-phishing-kali365-microsoft365-access-tokens/
ATT&CKT1564.008 T1114.001
Data sources
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType in~ ("New-InboxRule","Set-InboxRule","Update-InboxRules","UpdateInboxRules")
| extend Raw = tolower(tostring(RawEventData))
| where Raw has_any ("spam","phish","click","link","sharepoint")
| where Raw has_any ("movetofolder","markasread","deletemessage","junkemail")
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, IPAddress, ActionType, ObjectName, RawEventData
| order by Timestamp desc
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where Operation in~ ("New-InboxRule","Set-InboxRule","UpdateInboxRules")
| extend params = tolower(tostring(Parameters))
| where params has_any ("spam","phish","click","link","sharepoint")
| where params has_any ("movetofolder","markasread","deletemessage","junk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, ClientIP, Operation, OfficeWorkload, Parameters
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
index=o365 sourcetype="o365:management:activity" Operation IN ("New-InboxRule","Set-InboxRule","UpdateInboxRules")
| eval params=lower(_raw)
| where like(params,"%spam%") OR like(params,"%phish%") OR like(params,"%click%") OR like(params,"%link%") OR like(params,"%sharepoint%")
| where like(params,"%movetofolder%") OR like(params,"%markasread%") OR like(params,"%deletemessage%") OR like(params,"%junk%")
| table _time, UserId, ClientIP, Operation, Parameters
| sort - _time
[LLM] Attacker device registration in victim Entra tenant after device-code compromise Installation Medium
Hunts Entra ID 'Add registered device' / device-join audit events that Kali365 operators used to register attacker-controlled devices into compromised tenants, extending persistent access beyond the stolen token. High-value when correlated to a recent device-code sign-in or an anomalous source IP. Rationale: Targets Arctic Wolf's reported post-access step of registering new devices into the victim's Microsoft environment to extend access. Device-registration audit operations are the canonical telemetry for T1098.005 and are corroborated across the campaign write-ups. Cross-checked against: • https://arcticwolf.com/resources/blog/token-bingo-dont-let-your-code-be-the-winner/ • https://therecord.media/fbi-warns-of-kali365-phishing-attacks
ATT&CKT1098.005 T1078.004
Data sources
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where Application has "Entra" or Application has "Azure Active Directory"
| where ActionType has_any ("Add registered device","Register device","Add device","Add registered owner to device")
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, IPAddress, CountryCode, ActionType, ObjectName, ActivityObjects, RawEventData
| order by Timestamp desc
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where OperationName has_any ("Add registered device","Register device","Add device")
| where Result == "success"
| extend Initiator = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| extend InitiatorIP = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.ipAddress)
| extend TargetDevice = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, Initiator, InitiatorIP, TargetDevice, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Entra ID Device Registration Following Device-Code Compromise (Kali365)

[LLM] Microsoft 365 sign-in from Kali365 phishing infrastructure IPs Command & Control High
Alerts on any Entra/M365 sign-in sourced from confirmed Kali365 affiliate-panel infrastructure (216.203.20.95 and TLS-cert siblings). Arctic Wolf traced the campaign's seed infrastructure to 216.203.20.95; a sign-in from these IPs indicates an attacker replaying a stolen token or driving the device-code flow. Rationale: Pure IOC match on Arctic Wolf's confirmed seed IP 216.203.20.95 plus the pre-extracted sibling IPs; a tenant sign-in from these addresses is high-fidelity attacker activity. Named IOCs justify alerting tier. Cross-checked against: • https://arcticwolf.com/resources/blog/token-bingo-dont-let-your-code-be-the-winner/ • https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/05/22/kali365-microsoft-365-phishing-fbi-warning/

[LLM] Endpoint connection or DNS lookup to Kali365 Cookie Link AitM domains Command & Control High
Detects corporate endpoints resolving or connecting to Kali365-controlled domains (kali365.xyz, v2/api subdomains, duemineral.uk) used for the affiliate panel and the 'Cookie Link' adversary-in-the-middle mode that proxies victims to capture session cookies and tokens. Any internal host touching these domains indicates phishing interaction or attacker tooling. Rationale: Direct IOC match on the pre-extracted Kali365 domains (kali365.xyz and subdomains, duemineral.uk) tied to the affiliate panel and Cookie Link AitM proxy. An internal endpoint touching these is unambiguous phishing/C2 interaction; wildcard *.kali365.xyz catches new subdomains. Cross-checked against: • https://arcticwolf.com/resources/blog/token-bingo-dont-let-your-code-be-the-winner/ • https://hackread.com/fbi-kali365-phishing-service-microsoft-365-account/

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:

            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web

     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",

           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",

         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("883d5d4a73b0ac8cf4f78fe46d8f4e76e21508872836f2b439af2de4a205128e", "09bb7e568e573497e22bfa3f36d71fe9d104899826608affedb25d988f391c85", "2fa6fc2199d3be55e240500d87e4484f39b9315bf336be25434f6716b8d28ec8") or SHA1 in~ ("883d5d4a73b0ac8cf4f78fe46d8f4e76e21508872836f2b439af2de4a205128e", "09bb7e568e573497e22bfa3f36d71fe9d104899826608affedb25d988f391c85", "2fa6fc2199d3be55e240500d87e4484f39b9315bf336be25434f6716b8d28ec8") or MD5 in~ ("883d5d4a73b0ac8cf4f78fe46d8f4e76e21508872836f2b439af2de4a205128e", "09bb7e568e573497e22bfa3f36d71fe9d104899826608affedb25d988f391c85", "2fa6fc2199d3be55e240500d87e4484f39b9315bf336be25434f6716b8d28ec8")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("883d5d4a73b0ac8cf4f78fe46d8f4e76e21508872836f2b439af2de4a205128e", "09bb7e568e573497e22bfa3f36d71fe9d104899826608affedb25d988f391c85", "2fa6fc2199d3be55e240500d87e4484f39b9315bf336be25434f6716b8d28ec8") or SHA1 in~ ("883d5d4a73b0ac8cf4f78fe46d8f4e76e21508872836f2b439af2de4a205128e", "09bb7e568e573497e22bfa3f36d71fe9d104899826608affedb25d988f391c85", "2fa6fc2199d3be55e240500d87e4484f39b9315bf336be25434f6716b8d28ec8") or MD5 in~ ("883d5d4a73b0ac8cf4f78fe46d8f4e76e21508872836f2b439af2de4a205128e", "09bb7e568e573497e22bfa3f36d71fe9d104899826608affedb25d988f391c85", "2fa6fc2199d3be55e240500d87e4484f39b9315bf336be25434f6716b8d28ec8")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["883d5d4a73b0ac8cf4f78fe46d8f4e76e21508872836f2b439af2de4a205128e", "09bb7e568e573497e22bfa3f36d71fe9d104899826608affedb25d988f391c85", "2fa6fc2199d3be55e240500d87e4484f39b9315bf336be25434f6716b8d28ec8"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Ghost CMS Content API SQL injection (CVE-2026-26980) admin key theft Exploitation Medium
Hunts unauthenticated SQL injection against the Ghost CMS Content API endpoint used in CVE-2026-26980 to read the Admin API key and poison articles. Targets the /ghost/api/*content* path carrying SQL keywords in the query string against web-server access logs. Rationale: Pivots on the exact CVE-2026-26980 attack surface — the Ghost Content API path (/ghost/api/.../content) combined with SQLi tokens in the query string — rather than a generic WAF SQLi rule. Cross-checked XLab and BleepingComputer write-ups confirming the unauthenticated Content API read primitive. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.xlab.qianxin.com/ghost-cms-mass-compromised-via-cve-2026-26980-now-fueling-clickfix-attacks/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/ghost-cms-sql-injection-flaw-exploited-in-large-scale-clickfix-campaign/
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb.All_Traffic
union isfuzzy=true
(W3CIISLog
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
 | where csUriStem has "/ghost/api/" and csUriStem has "content"
 | where csUriQuery has_any ("filter=","UNION","SELECT","sqlite_master","sleep(","ascii(")
 | project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, Path = csUriStem, Query = csUriQuery, Status = scStatus, UserAgent = csUserAgent, Src = "W3CIISLog"),
(AppServiceHTTPLogs
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
 | where CsUriStem has "/ghost/api/" and CsUriStem has "content"
 | where CsUriQuery has_any ("filter=","UNION","SELECT","sqlite_master","sleep(","ascii(")
 | project TimeGenerated, Computer = CsHost, cIP = CIp, Path = CsUriStem, Query = CsUriQuery, Status = ScStatus, UserAgent, Src = "AppServiceHTTPLogs")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Endpoint contacts Ghost-poisoning ClickFix loader/TDS/C2 domains Command & Control High
Hunts any internal host resolving or connecting to the Ghost ClickFix campaign's loader, Adspect cloaking/TDS, and Electron C2 domains (clo4shara.xyz, com-apps.cc, web-telegram.ug, etc.) or the staging IP 144.31.236.66. These indicators span the JavaScript loader fetch, fake-CAPTCHA delivery, and Grape Electron beacon. Rationale: Direct IOC sweep on the campaign's named loader/cloaking/C2 domains and staging IP, all confirmed across XLab and BleepingComputer. com-apps.cc added because Cloudflare blocked clo4shara.xyz and the actor rotated to it. Schema fix: Sentinel side now reads DnsEvents.Name/ClientIP and unions CommonSecurityLog for the IP indicator (DnsEvents has no IPAddresses column). Cross-checked against: • https://blog.xlab.qianxin.com/ghost-cms-mass-compromised-via-cve-2026-26980-now-fueling-clickfix-attacks/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/ghost-cms-sql-injection-flaw-exploited-in-large-scale-clickfix-campaign/

[LLM] ClickFix Run-dialog chain: explorer-spawned shell fetching ZIP dropper Delivery High
Hunts the ClickFix fake-CAPTCHA pasted-command pattern where explorer.exe (the Windows Run dialog) spawns cmd/powershell/mshta/curl that downloads a ZIP from the campaign domains or pulls a remote archive. This is the hands-on-keyboard-by-victim execution that bridges the poisoned web page to the local payload. Rationale: Anchors on the article's described ClickFix mechanics — a command pasted into the Windows Run dialog (parent=explorer.exe) that drops/extracts a ZIP — paired with the campaign C2 domains, which is far more specific than a generic explorer-spawns-shell rule. Distinct from the excluded encoded-PowerShell/Office-macro rules because the parent is the Run dialog and the predicate is the ZIP+domain combo. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.xlab.qianxin.com/ghost-cms-mass-compromised-via-cve-2026-26980-now-fueling-clickfix-attacks/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/ghost-cms-sql-injection-flaw-exploited-in-large-scale-clickfix-campaign/
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "explorer.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe","curl.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (c2)
   or (ProcessCommandLine has ".zip" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Invoke-WebRequest","iwr ","DownloadFile","Start-BitsTransfer","certutil","bitsadmin","curl "))
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent

   or (CommandLine has ".zip" and CommandLine has_any ("Invoke-WebRequest","iwr ","DownloadFile","Start-BitsTransfer","certutil","bitsadmin","curl "))

detection:
  parent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\explorer.exe'
  child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
  context:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'clo4shara.xyz'
      - 'com-apps.cc'
      - 'web-telegram.ug'
      - 'cloud-verification.com'
      - 'jalwat.com'
      - 'platecrumbs.com'
      - 'taketwolabs.com'
      - 'staticcloudflare.pro'

level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\explorer.exe OR *\Explorer.EXE) @Image:(*\cmd.exe OR *\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\mshta.exe OR *\curl.exe) @CommandLine:(*clo4shara.xyz* OR *com-apps.cc* OR *web-telegram.ug* OR *cloud-verification.com* OR *jalwat.com* OR *platecrumbs.com* OR *taketwolabs.com* OR *staticcloudflare.pro*)

[LLM] Ghost ClickFix payload execution: known hashes / UtilifySetup.exe Electron dropper Installation High
Alerts on execution or file-write of the campaign's confirmed payload hashes (DLL loaders / JS droppers) and the UtilifySetup.exe Inno Setup installer that drops the modified Grape Electron client. High-fidelity IOC match on the final-stage malware. Rationale: Hard IOC match on the five MD5s + SHA1 published by XLab and the UtilifySetup.exe Electron sample (named in XLab/BleepingComputer), making this an alerting-grade detection on the final dropped payload. Hash + named-binary precision keeps FPs near zero. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.xlab.qianxin.com/ghost-cms-mass-compromised-via-cve-2026-26980-now-fueling-clickfix-attacks/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/ghost-cms-sql-injection-flaw-exploited-in-large-scale-clickfix-campaign/
ATT&CKT1218.011 T1105 T1036.001

[LLM] Grape Electron client persistence via HKCU Run key (setLoginItemSettings) Installation Medium
Hunts the modified Grape desktop (Electron) client establishing persistence by writing an HKCU CurrentVersion\Run value pointing to UtilifySetup/Grape, the behavior of its setLoginItemSettings call. This is the autostart that survives reboot and re-launches the 30-second C2 beacon to web-telegram.ug. Rationale: Targets the article/XLab-described setLoginItemSettings persistence, which in practice writes an HKCU Run value pointing at the Grape/UtilifySetup Electron binary — a registry pivot distinct from the network and process UCs. The UtilifySetup/Grape value-data tokens keep it campaign-specific. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.xlab.qianxin.com/ghost-cms-mass-compromised-via-cve-2026-26980-now-fueling-clickfix-attacks/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/ghost-cms-sql-injection-flaw-exploited-in-large-scale-clickfix-campaign/
ATT&CKT1547.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryKey has_any (@"\CurrentVersion\Run", @"\CurrentVersion\RunOnce")
| where RegistryValueData has_any ("UtilifySetup","Grape")
   or (RegistryValueData has @"\AppData\Roaming\" and RegistryValueData endswith ".exe" and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("explorer.exe","msiexec.exe"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData
| order by Timestamp desc
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where RegistryKey has_any (@"\CurrentVersion\Run", @"\CurrentVersion\RunOnce")
| where RegistryValueData has_any ("UtilifySetup","Grape")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData
| order by TimeGenerated desc

// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-26980")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-26980")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688

    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.

        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("clo4shara.xyz", "cloud-verification.com", "jalwat.com", "com-apps.cc", "web-telegram.ug", "platecrumbs.com", "taketwolabs.com", "staticcloudflare.pro", "script-dev.buzz", "updatesecurity.pro")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9434fe686801742ef7d6da248fb0b900dc32208a", "5659292833ec421da11ebde005d9c9a8", "d30cc10d54ebc967c8538ff74f442eee", "18a7251ddde77ed24bc54700d84d9be1", "f280e12f51f996dae7fffc64a56ee527", "fceca579efcef09eb507c6ca977ea281") or SHA1 in~ ("9434fe686801742ef7d6da248fb0b900dc32208a", "5659292833ec421da11ebde005d9c9a8", "d30cc10d54ebc967c8538ff74f442eee", "18a7251ddde77ed24bc54700d84d9be1", "f280e12f51f996dae7fffc64a56ee527", "fceca579efcef09eb507c6ca977ea281") or MD5 in~ ("9434fe686801742ef7d6da248fb0b900dc32208a", "5659292833ec421da11ebde005d9c9a8", "d30cc10d54ebc967c8538ff74f442eee", "18a7251ddde77ed24bc54700d84d9be1", "f280e12f51f996dae7fffc64a56ee527", "fceca579efcef09eb507c6ca977ea281")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9434fe686801742ef7d6da248fb0b900dc32208a", "5659292833ec421da11ebde005d9c9a8", "d30cc10d54ebc967c8538ff74f442eee", "18a7251ddde77ed24bc54700d84d9be1", "f280e12f51f996dae7fffc64a56ee527", "fceca579efcef09eb507c6ca977ea281") or SHA1 in~ ("9434fe686801742ef7d6da248fb0b900dc32208a", "5659292833ec421da11ebde005d9c9a8", "d30cc10d54ebc967c8538ff74f442eee", "18a7251ddde77ed24bc54700d84d9be1", "f280e12f51f996dae7fffc64a56ee527", "fceca579efcef09eb507c6ca977ea281") or MD5 in~ ("9434fe686801742ef7d6da248fb0b900dc32208a", "5659292833ec421da11ebde005d9c9a8", "d30cc10d54ebc967c8538ff74f442eee", "18a7251ddde77ed24bc54700d84d9be1", "f280e12f51f996dae7fffc64a56ee527", "fceca579efcef09eb507c6ca977ea281")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["9434fe686801742ef7d6da248fb0b900dc32208a", "5659292833ec421da11ebde005d9c9a8", "d30cc10d54ebc967c8538ff74f442eee", "18a7251ddde77ed24bc54700d84d9be1", "f280e12f51f996dae7fffc64a56ee527", "fceca579efcef09eb507c6ca977ea281"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Lazarus DPAPILoader masquerading as Iassvc.dll loaded from non-System32 path Installation High
Hunts the RemotePE first-stage loader (DPAPILoader), which ships as a DLL named 'Iassvc.dll' to impersonate the legitimate Windows Internet Authentication Service library and is side-loaded from a writable, non-standard directory. The genuine Iassvc.dll only ever lives under System32/WinSxS, so an Iassvc.dll loaded or written elsewhere is the loader. Rationale: Anchored on the exact DPAPILoader artifact name 'Iassvc.dll' from the article cross-checked against Fox-IT's writeup; the legitimate Iassvc.dll (IAS service) only resides in System32, so a copy/load from any other path is high-fidelity for the side-load with near-zero benign collision. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.fox-it.com/2025/09/01/three-lazarus-rats-coming-for-your-cheese/ • https://thehackernews.com/2025/09/lazarus-group-expands-malware-arsenal.html • https://socprime.com/blog/detect-lazarus-attacks-using-three-new-rats/
ATT&CKT1574.002 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "iassvc.dll"
| where FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\System32\"
    and FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\SysWOW64\"
    and FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\WinSxS\"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName =~ "iassvc.dll"
| where TargetFilePath !has @"\Windows\System32\"
    and TargetFilePath !has @"\Windows\SysWOW64\"
    and TargetFilePath !has @"\Windows\WinSxS\"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] RemotePELoader HTTP C2 beacon to aes-secure.net Command & Control Medium
Hunts the RemotePELoader second stage contacting its command-and-control server 'aes-secure[.]net' over HTTP to fetch and execute the memory-only RemotePE core module. Because RemotePE is never written to disk, this network callout is one of the few durable artifacts of the intrusion. Rationale: Uses the exact C2 domain aes-secure[.]net named in the primary article; the loader chain (DPAPI-loaded RemotePELoader beaconing over HTTP for a memory-only stage) is corroborated by Fox-IT, but the specific domain surfaced only in the primary article — hence Medium confidence; treat as a watchlist IOC and confirm against the Fox-IT IOC table. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.fox-it.com/2025/09/01/three-lazarus-rats-coming-for-your-cheese/ • https://thehackernews.com/2025/09/lazarus-group-expands-malware-arsenal.html

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DnsQuery has "aes-secure.net"
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName, DnsResponseCodeName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] RemotePE/PondRAT seven-pass file overwrite then rename and delete (anti-forensic wipe) Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the distinctive secure-deletion routine shared by RemotePE, PondRAT and POOLRAT: each target file is overwritten with constant bytes seven times, then renamed, then deleted. This surfaces as a single process performing many repeated writes to the same path followed by a rename/delete of that path. Rationale: Targets the article's specific anti-forensic signature — seven constant-byte overwrites followed by rename-then-delete, explicitly tied to RemotePE/PondRAT/POOLRAT — expressed as a high-write-count-then-delete threshold per process+file; behavioral/threshold-based, so no single-event Sigma is emitted. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.fox-it.com/2025/09/01/three-lazarus-rats-coming-for-your-cheese/ • https://thehackernews.com/2025/09/lazarus-group-expands-malware-arsenal.html
ATT&CKT1070.004 T1485
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileModified","FileRenamed","FileDeleted")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize Modifies = countif(ActionType == "FileModified"),
            Renames = countif(ActionType == "FileRenamed"),
            Deletes = countif(ActionType == "FileDeleted"),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
        by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessSHA256,
           InitiatingProcessId, FolderPath, FileName
| where Modifies >= 7 and (Renames >= 1 or Deletes >= 1)   // 7-pass constant-byte overwrite then rename/delete (RemotePE/PondRAT/POOLRAT secure-wipe)
| order by Modifies desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed","FileDeleted")
| summarize Writes = countif(EventType in ("FileModified","FileCreated")),
            Renames = countif(EventType == "FileRenamed"),
            Deletes = countif(EventType == "FileDeleted"),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
        by DvcHostname, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessId, TargetFilePath
| where Writes >= 7 and (Deletes >= 1 or Renames >= 1)   // 7-pass overwrite then rename/delete secure-wipe
| order by Writes desc
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, ContextProcessId, TargetFileName], function=count(as=writes))
| writes >= 7
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count(eval(Filesystem.action="modified")) as modifies count(eval(Filesystem.action="deleted")) as deletes count(eval(Filesystem.action="renamed")) as renames min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_id Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where modifies>=7 AND (deletes>=1 OR renames>=1) | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count(eval(Filesystem.action="modified")) as modifies count(eval(Filesystem.action="deleted")) as deletes count(eval(Filesystem.action="renamed")) as renames min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_id Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where modifies>=7 AND (deletes>=1 OR renames>=1) | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600

id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |

author: Clankerusecase

detection:

level: critical
