[LLM] cscript/wscript executing a script from .laravel_locale temp directory Installation High
Hunts cscript.exe or wscript.exe invocations whose command line references a .laravel_locale path. The Snyk advisory describes the Windows execution chain as the malicious PHP helper writing an 8-hex-char .vbs into %TEMP%\.laravel_locale\ and launching it via cscript — pairing the canonical script interpreter with the stealer's unique staging directory yields a tight signal. Rationale: Snyk explicitly documents the Windows execution chain as a .vbs launcher under %TEMP%\.laravel_locale\. The compound (cscript|wscript) + .laravel_locale leaves no realistic benign matches — neither Windows nor any common dev tool stages scripts in a directory of that name. Captures parent process so triage shows the PHP runtime (php.exe / php-cgi) that originated the launch. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/laravel-lang-supply-chain-attack • https://snyk.io/blog/laravel-lang-supply-chain-advisory/

references:
  - https://snyk.io/blog/laravel-lang-supply-chain-advisory/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/23
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.005
  - attack.t1195.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: '.laravel_locale'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) (@EventID:1 OR @EventID:4688) @Image:(*\cscript.exe OR *\CScript.exe OR *\CSCRIPT.EXE OR *\wscript.exe OR *\WScript.exe OR *\WSCRIPT.EXE) @CommandLine:(*.laravel_locale* OR *.LARAVEL_LOCALE*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\(c|w)script\.exe$/i CommandLine=/\.laravel_locale/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent values(Processes.process_path) as path from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="cscript.exe" OR Processes.process_name="wscript.exe") Processes.process="*.laravel_locale*" by Processes.dest Processes.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent values(Processes.process_path) as path from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="cscript.exe" OR Processes.process_name="wscript.exe") Processes.process="*.laravel_locale*" by Processes.dest Processes.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
[LLM] Compromised laravel-lang Composer package: helpers.php in vendor tree Delivery High
Hunts the file write or presence of src/helpers.php under vendor/laravel-lang/{lang,http-statuses,attributes,actions}/. A legitimate localization package has no reason to ship an autoload-files helper, so any host whose Composer cache contains this file pulled a poisoned tag during the May 22-23 2026 incident and should be treated as compromised until the package is rolled back and credentials rotated. Rationale: The Snyk detection guidance explicitly tells defenders to inspect vendor/laravel-lang/*/ for the presence of src/helpers.php — legitimate releases of these four localization packages do not ship a helpers file or use autoload.files. The package-name regex narrows to the four named-compromised packages (lang, http-statuses, attributes, actions) per the affected-versions table, avoiding stray matches on other laravel-lang/* repos. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/Laravel-Lang/http-statuses/issues/277 • https://gbhackers.com/compromise-laravel-lang-packages/ • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/laravel-lang-supply-chain-attack
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath has "vendor\\laravel-lang\\" or FolderPath has "vendor/laravel-lang/"
| where FileName =~ "helpers.php"
| extend Package = extract(@"laravel-lang[\\/](lang|http-statuses|attributes|actions)", 1, FolderPath)
| where isnotempty(Package)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, Package, SHA256, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath has "vendor/laravel-lang/" or TargetFilePath has @"vendor\laravel-lang\"
| where TargetFileName =~ "helpers.php"
| extend Package = extract(@"laravel-lang[\\/](lang|http-statuses|attributes|actions)", 1, TargetFilePath)
| where isnotempty(Package)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, Package, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Compromised Laravel-Lang Composer Helper File on Disk
id: a02c4b7f-5e67-8d1b-e02f-5678901234ef
description: Detects creation of src/helpers.php under vendor/laravel-lang/{lang,http-statuses,attributes,actions} - the malicious autoload-files entry injected during the May 2026 Laravel-Lang Composer supply-chain compromise.
references:
  - https://snyk.io/blog/laravel-lang-supply-chain-advisory/
  - https://github.com/Laravel-Lang/http-statuses/issues/277
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/laravel-lang-supply-chain-attack
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/23
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1546
logsource:
  category: file_event
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|contains|all:
      - 'vendor'
      - 'laravel-lang'
      - 'src'
      - 'helpers.php'
  condition: selection
level: medium
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\vendor\laravel-lang\*\src\helpers.php OR *\VENDOR\LARAVEL-LANG\*\SRC\HELPERS.PHP)) OR (source:linux.auditd @file.path:(*/vendor/laravel-lang/*/src/helpers.php))
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/vendor[\\\/]laravel-lang[\\\/](lang|http-statuses|attributes|actions)[\\\/]src[\\\/]helpers\.php$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths values(Filesystem.process_name) as procs from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*/vendor/laravel-lang/*/src/helpers.php" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\vendor\\laravel-lang\\*\\src\\helpers.php") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| rex field=paths "laravel-lang[\\/](?<package>lang|http-statuses|attributes|actions)"
| where isnotnull(package)
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths values(Filesystem.process_name) as procs from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*/vendor/laravel-lang/*/src/helpers.php" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\vendor\\laravel-lang\\*\\src\\helpers.php") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| rex field=paths "laravel-lang[\\/](?<package>lang|http-statuses|attributes|actions)"
| where isnotnull(package)
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("") or RemoteUrl has_any ("flipboxstudio.info")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["flipboxstudio.info"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Stealers / wallet drainers read keystore.json, MetaMask, Exodus, Atomic, Phantom data.
ATT&CKT1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Ethereum\keystore\", @"\Bitcoin\", @"\Exodus\", @"\Electrum\wallets\", @"\MetaMask\", @"\Phantom\", @"\Atomic\Local Storage\")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Ethereum\keystore\", @"\Bitcoin\",
                                  @"\Exodus\", @"\Electrum\wallets\",
                                  @"\MetaMask\", @"\Phantom\",
                                  @"\Atomic\Local Storage\")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe",

title: Crypto-Wallet Keystore Access by Non-Wallet Process
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d02
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers / wallet drainers read keystore files from MetaMask,
    Exodus, Atomic, Phantom, Bitcoin, Electrum, Ethereum-cli wallets.
    Filtering out the legitimate wallet binaries leaves only attacker
    activity.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1005/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1005
    - attack.collection
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Ethereum\keystore\'
            - '\Bitcoin\'
            - '\Exodus\'
            - '\Electrum\wallets\'
            - '\MetaMask\'
            - '\Phantom\'
            - '\Atomic\Local Storage\'
    filter_legit:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\MetaMask.exe'
            - '\Exodus.exe'
            - '\Atomic.exe'
            - '\electrum.exe'
            - '\Bitcoin.exe'
            - '\Phantom.exe'
    condition: selection_path and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
    - Backup software
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Ethereum\keystore\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Bitcoin\wallet.dat"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Exodus\exodus.wallet*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Electrum\wallets\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\MetaMask\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Phantom\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Atomic\Local Storage\*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Ethereum\keystore\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Bitcoin\wallet.dat"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Exodus\exodus.wallet*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Electrum\wallets\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\MetaMask\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Phantom\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Atomic\Local Storage\*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"

          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("bba2e443dc7ff1f8704f52a5375383e3f4f643b8", "a5ea2e8fa92ccf29cdb1d2dadbeb27722b2bff37", "556d2b335d4d6d92139822017ee461b668afe375") or SHA1 in~ ("bba2e443dc7ff1f8704f52a5375383e3f4f643b8", "a5ea2e8fa92ccf29cdb1d2dadbeb27722b2bff37", "556d2b335d4d6d92139822017ee461b668afe375") or MD5 in~ ("bba2e443dc7ff1f8704f52a5375383e3f4f643b8", "a5ea2e8fa92ccf29cdb1d2dadbeb27722b2bff37", "556d2b335d4d6d92139822017ee461b668afe375")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("bba2e443dc7ff1f8704f52a5375383e3f4f643b8", "a5ea2e8fa92ccf29cdb1d2dadbeb27722b2bff37", "556d2b335d4d6d92139822017ee461b668afe375") or SHA1 in~ ("bba2e443dc7ff1f8704f52a5375383e3f4f643b8", "a5ea2e8fa92ccf29cdb1d2dadbeb27722b2bff37", "556d2b335d4d6d92139822017ee461b668afe375") or MD5 in~ ("bba2e443dc7ff1f8704f52a5375383e3f4f643b8", "a5ea2e8fa92ccf29cdb1d2dadbeb27722b2bff37", "556d2b335d4d6d92139822017ee461b668afe375")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["bba2e443dc7ff1f8704f52a5375383e3f4f643b8", "a5ea2e8fa92ccf29cdb1d2dadbeb27722b2bff37", "556d2b335d4d6d92139822017ee461b668afe375"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] PHP/web-server process beaconing to flipboxstudio.info Command & Control High
Detects php-fpm, php-cli, or web-server worker processes resolving or connecting to flipboxstudio.info — the first-stage C2 used by the trojanised laravel-lang packages to pull the ~5,900-line PHP stealer. Article-specific because the C2 host is hardcoded into src/helpers.php. Rationale: flipboxstudio.info is the C2 host explicitly named in the article and pre-extracted IOC list; a PHP/web-server worker resolving it during request handling is the textbook auto-loaded helpers.php beacon. Process-context filter keeps FPs near-zero.

| order by Timestamp desc

)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] php-fpm/php-cli spawning cscript.exe with VBS launcher (Laravel-Lang dropper) Installation High
Detects the Windows-specific dropper behaviour of the trojanised laravel-lang helpers.php — a PHP request-handling process spawns cscript.exe to run a VBScript launcher. Article explicitly notes 'delivers a Visual Basic Script launcher on Windows and runs it via cscript.' Rationale: Article literally states 'the dropper delivers a Visual Basic Script launcher on Windows and runs it via cscript.' php.exe → cscript.exe is an extremely rare parent/child pair outside this attack chain; pairing with .vbs argument makes it almost FP-free.

[LLM] Mass credential-file fan-out reads from single PHP/www-data process Actions on Objectives High
Detects a single PHP/web-server worker process touching multiple high-value credential files within seconds — the fan-out signature of the ~5,900-line laravel-lang stealer's 15 collector modules (AWS, SSH, Kube, .env, wp-config, .git-credentials, browser vaults). Rationale: Article lists 15 specialist collector modules targeting AWS/SSH/Kube/.env/wp-config/.git-credentials/browser Login Data/wallets/password managers — a single PHP worker reading ≥5 of these within 5 minutes is the unmistakable stealer fan-out shape and would never happen during normal request handling. Verbatim path strings (@"\.aws\credentials") avoid the prior KQL escape failure.

| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed") or ActionType startswith "File"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php.exe","php-cgi.exe","php-fpm.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","w3wp.exe","php","php-fpm","httpd","nginx","apache2")

| summarize FileCount = dcount(strcat(FolderPath, FileName)),

| where SpanSeconds <= 300
| order by LastSeen desc

[LLM] AES-encrypted exfil POST to flipboxstudio.info/exfil Actions on Objectives High
Targets the second-stage exfil channel — HTTP POST from a PHP/web-server worker to flipboxstudio.info/exfil carrying AES-256 encrypted collected credentials. Article explicitly: 'encrypts the results with AES-256 and sends them to flipboxstudio[.]info/exfil.' Rationale: Article gives the exact exfil URL pattern 'flipboxstudio[.]info/exfil' — combining the host, /exfil path, and POST method from a PHP worker is essentially a deterministic IOC match.
ATT&CKT1041 T1560.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "flipboxstudio.info/exfil" or (RemoteUrl has "flipboxstudio.info" and InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php.exe","php-fpm.exe","php-cgi.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","w3wp.exe","php","php-fpm","httpd","nginx","apache2"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
(union isfuzzy=true
  (CommonSecurityLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d) | where (RequestURL contains "flipboxstudio.info/exfil") or (DestinationHostName =~ "flipboxstudio.info" and RequestMethod =~ "POST") | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, SentBytes, ReceivedBytes, SourceUserName),
  (W3CIISLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d) | where csUriStem contains "/exfil" and csHost has "flipboxstudio" | project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csMethod, csUriStem, csUserAgent),
  (ImWebSession | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d) | where Url has "flipboxstudio.info/exfil" or (DstHostname =~ "flipboxstudio.info" and HttpMethod =~ "POST") | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, Url, HttpMethod, HttpRequestBodyBytes)
)

[LLM] PHP/web-server worker querying cloud metadata IMDS endpoints Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects php-fpm/httpd/nginx/w3wp processes connecting to 169.254.169.254 (AWS/Azure IMDS) or metadata.google.internal — used by the laravel-lang stealer to grab IAM roles, instance identity documents, and GCP/Azure access tokens during the discovery+credential-access phases. Rationale: Article specifies the stealer 'queries cloud metadata endpoints' for IAM roles, GCP application default creds, and Azure access tokens. PHP request-handling processes calling IMDS is non-existent in normal web traffic — at most one app per fleet does this, easy to allowlist.
ATT&CKT1552.005 T1580
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (RemoteIP == "169.254.169.254" or RemoteUrl has "metadata.google.internal" or RemoteUrl has "169.254.169.254")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php.exe","php-cgi.exe","php-fpm.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","w3wp.exe","php","php-fpm","httpd","nginx","apache2")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
(union isfuzzy=true
  (DnsEvents | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d) | where Name has "metadata.google.internal" | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType),
  (CommonSecurityLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d) | where DestinationIP == "169.254.169.254" or DestinationHostName has "metadata.google.internal" | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceHostName, DestinationIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, ProcessName, SourceUserName)
)

[LLM] helpers.php write under vendor/laravel-lang and composer autoload tampering Installation High
File-integrity detection for the persistence vector — src/helpers.php inside vendor/laravel-lang/* being created or modified, or vendor/composer/autoload_files.php being rewritten to reference it. Article confirms 'this file is registered in the composer.json under autoload.files' so the backdoor re-runs every PHP request. Rationale: Article quote: 'this file [src/helpers.php] is registered in the composer.json under autoload.files, the backdoor is executed automatically on every PHP request.' Watching writes to vendor/laravel-lang/*/helpers.php and autoload_files.php is the cleanest persistence detection because it's filesystem-deterministic, language-agnostic across Windows/Linux, and surfaces affected hosts even if C2 is sinkholed.
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where (FolderPath has "vendor" and FolderPath has "laravel-lang" and FileName =~ "helpers.php")
   or (FolderPath has "vendor" and FolderPath has "composer" and FileName =~ "autoload_files.php")
   or (FileName =~ "composer.lock")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed","FileCreate","FileWrite")
| where (TargetFilePath has "vendor" and TargetFilePath has "laravel-lang" and TargetFileName =~ "helpers.php")
   or (TargetFilePath has "vendor/composer" and TargetFileName =~ "autoload_files.php")
   or TargetFileName =~ "composer.lock"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| order by files desc

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,

// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"

[LLM] LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin CVE-2026-48172 — redisAble exploit request in HTTP/access logs Exploitation High
Hunts the exact LiteSpeed-provided IOC: HTTP requests carrying the cPanel JSON-API parameter cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble against the user-end LiteSpeed plugin. Any successful 2xx hit on this parameter against a server running plugin 2.3–2.4.4 is post-exploitation evidence and should be treated as a confirmed root-level compromise candidate. Rationale: Anchored on the exact vendor-supplied grep IOC from the LiteSpeed advisory (cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble) — a string that has zero legitimate use case in normal cPanel traffic outside this exploitation path. Cross-checked against the GitHub Advisory (GHSA-fxrh-cwjh-m33v), NVD entry, and cybersecuritynews.com / systemtek.co.uk write-ups; all four corroborate the same IOC and affected version range 2.3–2.4.4. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fxrh-cwjh-m33v • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-48172 • https://cybersecuritynews.com/litespeed-cpanel-plugin-0-day-exploited/ • https://www.systemtek.co.uk/2026/05/litespeed-user-end-cpanel-plugin-privilege-escalation-vulnerability-cve-2026-48172/
ATT&CKT1190 T1068
Data sourcesWeb.Web
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble" or AdditionalFields has "cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc
let ioc = "cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble";
union isfuzzy=true
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where RequestURL has ioc or Message has ioc
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceTable="CommonSecurityLog", DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, DestinationHostName=coalesce(DestinationHostName, DeviceExternalID), RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, DeviceAction),
(Syslog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where ProcessName in~ ("httpd","apache2","lsws","cpanellogd","cpsrvd","litespeed") or Facility in~ ("local6","daemon")
  | where SyslogMessage has ioc
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceTable="Syslog", DeviceVendor="cPanel/LiteSpeed", DeviceProduct=ProcessName, SourceIP=extract(@"([0-9]{1,3}(?:\.[0-9]{1,3}){3})", 1, SyslogMessage), DestinationHostName=HostName, RequestURL=SyslogMessage, RequestClientApplication="", DeviceAction=""),
(W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where csUriQuery has ioc or csUriStem has ioc
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceTable="W3CIISLog", DeviceVendor="IIS", DeviceProduct="web", SourceIP=cIP, DestinationHostName=Computer, RequestURL=strcat(csUriStem,"?",csUriQuery), RequestClientApplication=csUserAgent, DeviceAction=tostring(scStatus))
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin CVE-2026-48172 — root-privileged child spawned by lsws/cpsrvd worker Installation High
Post-exploitation pivot for CVE-2026-48172. Hunts shell, scripting, or LOLBin children executed with effective UID 0 whose parent is the LiteSpeed or cPanel JSON-API worker process (lsws, cpsrvd, lswsctrld, queueprocd). The vuln's outcome is 'arbitrary scripts as root' — this catches the script execution itself even when the upstream HTTP log was rotated or scrubbed. Rationale: Maps the vuln's stated outcome ('execute arbitrary scripts as root' via lsws.redisAble) to its inevitable on-host artefact: a root-uid child of the LiteSpeed/cPanel daemon. The parent-process list (lsws/cpsrvd/queueprocd/lscmctl) comes from the LiteSpeed plugin layout under /usr/local/lsws/ called out in the article's mitigation command and corroborated by the cPanel daemon naming convention documented in cybersecuritynews.com's write-up. Catches the exploit even when WAF/access logs are missing. Cross-checked against: • https://cybersecuritynews.com/litespeed-cpanel-plugin-0-day-exploited/ • https://www.gotekky.com/guides/security/litespeed-user-end-cpanel-plugin-privilege-escalation-2026/ • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fxrh-cwjh-m33v
ATT&CKT1068 T1059.004 T1505.003

| where FileName in~ ("bash","sh","dash","zsh","perl","python","python3","php","curl","wget","nc","ncat","socat","chmod","chown","useradd","usermod","crontab","base64","openssl")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("redisAble","/tmp/","/dev/shm/","-c \"","bash -i","/dev/tcp/","chmod +x","curl -fsSL","wget -qO")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ParentImage=InitiatingProcessFolderPath, ParentCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ChildImage=FolderPath, ChildCmd=ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc

let susp_children = dynamic(["bash","sh","dash","zsh","perl","python","python3","php","curl","wget","nc","ncat","socat","chmod","chown","useradd","usermod","crontab","base64","openssl"]);

Laravel-Lang Supply Chain Attack: Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten to Steal CI Secrets

StepSecurity
2026-05-23 9 use cases 2 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

On May 22, 2026, an attacker with push access to the Laravel-Lang GitHub organization rewrote every git tag across multiple popular Composer packages within a single 15 minute window. Anyone running composer update or installing fresh against laravel-lang/http-statuses, laravel-lang/actions, or laravel-lang/attributes now pulls a payload that exfiltrates CI secrets to a typosquatted attacker domain. StepSecurity confirmed end to end exploitation in an isolated runner and has filed security issues in all four repositories.

ATT&CKT1190 T1195.002

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] GitHub bulk git tag force-push by single actor across multiple org repos
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] PHP CLI drops hidden /tmp dropper artefacts (Laravel-Lang autoload payload) · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Laravel-Lang Supply Chain Attack: Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Re
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Egress to typosquatted C2 flipboxstudio.info (Laravel-Lang Composer SC) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Orphaned process (ppid=1) executing from /tmp hidden hex path (post-dropper stage-2)
[LLM] Egress to typosquatted C2 flipboxstudio.info (Laravel-Lang Composer SC) Command & Control High
Hunts DNS or HTTP(S) callbacks to flipboxstudio.info, the attacker-controlled typosquat of the legitimate flipboxstudio.com used as the stage-1 fetch endpoint (/payload) and stage-2 exfiltration sink (/exfil) by the May 2026 Laravel-Lang Composer supply-chain dropper. Single-IOC alerter — exact-domain match, near-zero FP expectation. Rationale: Anchors on the exact attacker-controlled domain `flipboxstudio.info` named verbatim in the IOC block as both the stage-1 GET endpoint (/payload) and stage-2 POST exfil endpoint (/exfil). The domain is a brand-new typosquat of flipboxstudio.com with no legitimate business use — any hit is high-fidelity.

[LLM] PHP CLI drops hidden /tmp dropper artefacts (Laravel-Lang autoload payload) Installation High
Hunts PHP CLI processes (typically from a composer-driven vendor/autoload.php boot) creating files under /tmp/.laravel_locale/<12-hex>.php or /tmp/.<8-hex> matching the exact dropper naming scheme generated by bin2hex(random_bytes(6)) in the malicious src/helpers.php. Combines hidden-path masquerade with the specific php-as-parent shape. Rationale: Anchors on the exact `/tmp/.laravel_locale/<12 hex chars>.php` PHP loader path and `/tmp/.<8 hex chars>` ELF path named in the IOC block, combined with the php-CLI parent shape that follows from `vendor/autoload.php` invoking the malicious helpers.php. The hex-length pattern matches the article's explicit `bin2hex(random_bytes(6))` naming generator.
ATT&CKT1564.001 T1105 T1059.004 T1204.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName matches regex @"^php[0-9]?$" or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php-cli","php-fpm")
| where FolderPath startswith "/tmp/.laravel_locale" 
   or (FolderPath == "/tmp" and FileName matches regex @"^\.[a-f0-9]{6,12}$")
   or (FolderPath startswith "/tmp/." and FileName matches regex @"^[a-f0-9]{6,12}\.php$")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated"
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"/php[0-9]?$" or ActingProcessName endswith "/php-cli"
| where TargetFilePath startswith "/tmp/.laravel_locale/" 
   or TargetFilePath matches regex @"^/tmp/\.[a-f0-9]{6,12}$"
   or TargetFilePath matches regex @"^/tmp/\.[a-f0-9]+/[a-f0-9]{6,12}\.php$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: PHP CLI Drops Hidden Payload to /tmp (Laravel-Lang Composer SC)
id: 4c1bd2e5-9a47-4f8e-8d3a-7c8b2e3f4a5d
description: Detects a php process writing a hidden dropper to /tmp/.laravel_locale/<hex>.php or /tmp/.<hex>, matching the Laravel-Lang Composer supply-chain helpers.php payload that uses bin2hex(random_bytes(6)) for filename generation.

[LLM] Orphaned process (ppid=1) executing from /tmp hidden hex path (post-dropper stage-2) Actions on Objectives High
Hunts processes reparented to init/systemd (ppid=1) whose image or command-line resolves to /tmp/.<6-12 hex chars> — the exact reparenting + execute-from-deleted-path shape left behind by the Laravel-Lang stage-2 loader after it backgrounds via `php "$f" > /dev/null 2>&1 &` and rm-deletes its own dropper files. Visible in process telemetry even after the file is unlinked. Rationale: Anchors on the article's explicit process IOCs: 'an orphaned php process with ppid=1' and 'an orphaned unnamed ELF process with ppid=1, executing from a now deleted path under /tmp'. Combines the reparent-to-init shape with the /tmp/.<hex> path generated by bin2hex(random_bytes(6)). Survives the self-delete because process metadata is captured at exec time.
ATT&CKT1036.005 T1564.001 T1070.004 T1620
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("systemd","init")
| where (FolderPath matches regex @"^/tmp/\.[a-f0-9]{6,12}$")
   or (FileName matches regex @"^php[0-9]?$" and ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/tmp/\.[a-f0-9]{6,12}(\.php)?")
   or (FolderPath startswith "/tmp/.laravel_locale")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, ProcessId, InitiatingProcessId
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("systemd","init") or ParentProcessId == 1
| where (ActingProcessName matches regex @"^/tmp/\.[a-f0-9]{6,12}$")
   or (ActingProcessName endswith "/php" and ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/tmp/\.[a-f0-9]{6,12}(\.php)?")
   or (ActingProcessName startswith "/tmp/.laravel_locale")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessId, ActingProcessId
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Orphaned PHP/ELF from /tmp Hidden Hex Path (Laravel-Lang Composer SC Stage-2)

description: Detects a process whose parent is systemd/init (reparented ppid=1) running from /tmp/.<hex> or whose command line references the Laravel-Lang stage-2 hidden dropper path. The article notes both an orphaned php and an unnamed ELF process executing from a now-deleted /tmp path.

(#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 OR #event_simpleName=SyntheticProcessRollup2) ParentBaseFileName=/^(systemd|init)$/i

[LLM] GitHub bulk git tag force-push by single actor across multiple org repos Delivery Medium
Hunts the org-wide tag-rewrite shape that defined the initial-access step: one GitHub actor force-pushing tags across multiple repositories in the same org within a short window (the Laravel-Lang attacker rewrote 502+ tags across four repos in 88 minutes). Combine with commit-author imposter signature 'Your Name' / 'you@example.com'. Rationale: Anchors on the article's exact shape: 'every git tag across multiple popular Composer packages within a single 15 minute window', 502 tags rewritten in one repo, four repos hit in 88 minutes, all by the same compromised credential. The commit-author imposter strings 'Your Name' / 'you@example.com' are also called out verbatim. Sentinel/Defender/Falcon are left empty because GitHub audit telemetry is not in their canonical schemas — Splunk and Datadog (via the GitHub integration) are the realistic shipping paths.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1078 T1098
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
source:github (@action:git.push OR @action:git.create) @git.ref:refs/tags/*
CLOUD
index=* sourcetype IN ("github:audit","github_audit_log","github:enterprise:audit") (action="git.push" OR action="git.create" OR action="protected_branch.policy_override") ref="refs/tags/*"
| eval repo_org=mvindex(split(repo,"/"),0)
| stats min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen dc(repo) as repo_count dc(ref) as tag_count values(repo) as repos values(ref) as refs by actor, repo_org
| eval window_seconds = last_seen - first_seen
| where tag_count >= 10 AND repo_count >= 2 AND window_seconds <= 3600
| eval window_minutes = round(window_seconds/60, 1)
| convert ctime(first_seen) ctime(last_seen)
| sort - tag_count
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Supply Chain Attack Targets Laravel-Lang Packages with Credential Stealer

Aikido
2026-05-23 11 use cases 5 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Attackers injected a credential stealer into 200+ versions of popular Laravel-Lang packages, delivering a credential stealer targeting cloud keys, SSH keys, browsers, crypto wallets and more. Category: Vulnerabilities & Threats

ATT&CKT1021.001 T1176 T1190 T1195.002 T1555.003
Domainsflipboxstudio.info

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Composer install of malicious helpers.php in laravel-lang vendor package
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Supply Chain Attack Targets Laravel-Lang Packages with Credential Stealer
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] cscript.exe launching .vbs from .laravel_locale temp directory · [LLM] Stealer or VBS launcher dropped into .laravel_locale temp directory · Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] C2 egress to flipboxstudio.info from Laravel-Lang composer dropper · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process
[LLM] C2 egress to flipboxstudio.info from Laravel-Lang composer dropper Command & Control High
Detects any HTTP/DNS contact with the hard-coded C2 domain flipboxstudio.info (decoded from integer array in the malicious src/helpers.php). Both the /payload fetch (stage-2 stealer download) and /exfil (AES-256 encrypted credential exfil) hit the same FQDN, so any resolution or connection is unambiguously malicious. Rationale: Anchored on the article's named C2 domain flipboxstudio.info plus the /payload and /exfil URL paths quoted verbatim. Corroborated by https://socket.dev/blog/malicious-packagist-packages-disguised-as-laravel-utilities and https://gbhackers.com/malicious-laravel-packages/. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/malicious-packagist-packages-disguised-as-laravel-utilities • https://gbhackers.com/malicious-laravel-packages/ • https://cybersecuritynews.com/malicious-packages-disguised-as-laravel-utilities/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041 T1132.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let C2Host = "flipboxstudio.info";
union isfuzzy=true
(
  DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
  | where RemoteUrl has C2Host or RemoteUrl has "flipboxstudio.info/payload" or RemoteUrl has "flipboxstudio.info/exfil"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName,
            InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
            RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, ActionType
),
(
  DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
  | where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse" or ActionType == "InboundConnectionAccepted"
  | where AdditionalFields has C2Host
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
            InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
            RemoteIP, AdditionalFields, ActionType
)
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let C2Host = "flipboxstudio.info";
union isfuzzy=true
(
  DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
  | where Name has C2Host
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, Result
),
(
  CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
  | where RequestURL has C2Host or DestinationHostName has C2Host
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, RequestURL, DestinationHostName, SourceUserName, RequestClientApplication
),
(
  ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
  | where Url has C2Host or HttpHostName has C2Host
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, Url, HttpHostName, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] cscript.exe launching .vbs from .laravel_locale temp directory Installation High
Detects the Windows arm of the Laravel-Lang dropper: the malicious src/helpers.php writes an 8-hex-character .vbs launcher into <temp>\.laravel_locale\ and executes it silently via cscript. Process tree is php/php-fpm/php-cgi (or anything that triggered composer autoload) → cscript.exe with a .vbs path containing `.laravel_locale`. Rationale: Anchored on two article-quoted strings together: `<tmp>/.laravel_locale/<8 random hex chars>.vbs` and the explicit `runs the payload silently via cscript` Windows-launcher behaviour. The 8-hex regex makes this near-zero-FP. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/malicious-packagist-packages-disguised-as-laravel-utilities • https://gbhackers.com/malicious-laravel-packages/
ATT&CKT1059.005 T1105 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let LookbackDays = 14d;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where FileName =~ "cscript.exe" or FileName =~ "wscript.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has @".laravel_locale"
   and ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\.laravel_locale[\\/][0-9a-f]{8}\.vbs"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 14d;
union isfuzzy=true
(
  SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where NewProcessName endswith "\\cscript.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\wscript.exe"
  | where CommandLine has ".laravel_locale" and CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\.laravel_locale[\\\\/][0-9a-f]{8}\.vbs"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
),
(
  ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
  | where ActingProcessName endswith "cscript.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "wscript.exe"
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has ".laravel_locale"
     and ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\.laravel_locale[\\\\/][0-9a-f]{8}\.vbs"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Composer install of malicious helpers.php in laravel-lang vendor package Delivery Medium
Detects composer (or any file mover) writing a src/helpers.php file under vendor/laravel-lang/{lang,attributes,http-statuses}/ — the article confirms this file does not exist in the legitimate packages and was injected by the attacker via fork-tag commits. Catches the supply-chain payload at composer-install time, before the dropper detonates. Rationale: Anchored on the article-quoted file name (`src/helpers.php`) plus the three affected package names verbatim (`laravel-lang/lang`, `laravel-lang/attributes`, `laravel-lang/http-statuses`). The file is novel to the malicious tags, so any write is high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/malicious-packagist-packages-disguised-as-laravel-utilities • https://thehackernews.com/2026/03/fake-laravel-packages-on-packagist.html
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.004

| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)

| where FileName =~ "helpers.php"
| where FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)[\\\\/]vendor[\\\\/]laravel-lang[\\\\/](lang|attributes|http-statuses)[\\\\/]src[\\\\/]?$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc

ImFileEvent

[LLM] Stealer or VBS launcher dropped into .laravel_locale temp directory Installation High
Detects file creation inside <temp>\.laravel_locale\ matching the article's exact naming patterns: 12-hex-character .php (the ~5,900-line stealer fetched from flipboxstudio.info/payload) or 8-hex-character .vbs (Windows cscript launcher). Catches the runtime dropper post-detonation, including the marker MD5 file that gates re-execution. Rationale: Anchored on the article's verbatim path patterns: `<tmp>/.laravel_locale/<md5_hash>` (32-hex marker), `<tmp>/.laravel_locale/<12 random hex chars>.php` (stealer body), `<tmp>/.laravel_locale/<8 random hex chars>.vbs` (Windows launcher). The directory name plus the hex-only filename regex makes near-zero-FP. Cross-checked with https://gbhackers.com/malicious-laravel-packages/. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/malicious-packagist-packages-disguised-as-laravel-utilities • https://gbhackers.com/malicious-laravel-packages/
ATT&CKT1105 T1036.005 T1140
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let LookbackDays = 14d;
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where FolderPath has @".laravel_locale" or FolderPath has @"/.laravel_locale/" or FolderPath has @"\\.laravel_locale\\"
| where (FileName matches regex @"(?i)^[0-9a-f]{12}\.php$")
     or (FileName matches regex @"(?i)^[0-9a-f]{8}\.vbs$")
     or (FileName matches regex @"(?i)^[0-9a-f]{32}$")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, FileSize,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 14d;
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath has ".laravel_locale"
| where (TargetFileName matches regex @"(?i)^[0-9a-f]{12}\.php$")
     or (TargetFileName matches regex @"(?i)^[0-9a-f]{8}\.vbs$")
     or (TargetFileName matches regex @"(?i)^[0-9a-f]{32}$")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSize, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest

| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

[LLM] Nezha CVE-2026-46716 exploit: POST /api/v1/cron with empty servers + CronCoverAll Exploitation High
Detects the exploit signature for Nezha Monitoring CVE-2026-46716 where a RoleMember submits a cron task with `cover=1` (CronCoverAll) and `servers=[]` to trigger the vacuous-true permission bypass in createCron. Targets the dashboard's web tier via reverse-proxy / WAF / IIS / App Service logs that capture POST bodies or at least the URI. Rationale: Targets the exact URI named in the GHSA advisory (`POST /api/v1/cron` gated by commonHandler not adminHandler) and the body shape that triggers the vacuous-true bypass (`servers=[]` + `cover=1`). The endpoint is rare under normal operation — admins create cron tasks occasionally, so even the URI alone is a strong pivot; body inspection (when WAF/proxy logs include it) elevates to deterministic. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-99gv-2m7h-3hh9 • https://github.com/nezhahq/nezha • https://nezha.wiki/en_US/
ATT&CKT1190 T1078 T1068
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Primary: WAF / proxy logs that capture request body in DeviceCustomString or RequestContext
let ExploitBodyPattern = @'(?is)"servers"\s*:\s*\[\s*\][^}]*"cover"\s*:\s*1|"cover"\s*:\s*1[^}]*"servers"\s*:\s*\[\s*\]';
union isfuzzy=true
(CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestMethod == "POST"
| where RequestURL endswith "/api/v1/cron"
| extend Body = strcat(coalesce(DeviceCustomString1, ""), " ", coalesce(DeviceCustomString2, ""), " ", coalesce(DeviceCustomString3, ""), " ", coalesce(RequestContext, ""), " ", coalesce(Message, ""))
| where Body matches regex ExploitBodyPattern or RequestURL has "cover=1"
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIP=SourceIP, Dst=DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, Body, RequestClientApplication, SourceUserName),
(W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csMethod == "POST"
| where csUriStem endswith "/api/v1/cron"
| where scStatus >= 200 and scStatus < 300
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIP=cIP, Dst=Computer, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csUserName, csUserAgent, scStatus),
(AppServiceHTTPLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where CsMethod == "POST"
| where CsUriStem endswith "/api/v1/cron"
| where ScStatus >= 200 and ScStatus < 300
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIP=CIp, Dst=CsHost, CsUriStem, CsUriQuery, CsUsername, UserAgent, ScStatus)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: 7c1b0e94-3a2f-4d6e-9b1a-46716cvebd01
status: experimental
description: Detects exploitation of Nezha Monitoring CVE-2026-46716 — a POST to /api/v1/cron whose body has the vacuous-permission-bypass shape (empty servers list combined with CronCoverAll=1). Any RoleMember authenticated request matching this body gets cross-tenant RCE on every monitored agent.

    - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-99gv-2m7h-3hh9

[LLM] nezha-agent spawning credential-access shell commands on Linux (post-RCE) Actions on Objectives High
Detects the post-exploitation footprint of Nezha CVE-2026-46716 on victim hosts: the nezha-agent process (typically running as root) executes a shell child that reads /etc/shadow or curls the cloud instance-metadata endpoint — exactly the PoC payload in the advisory. Targets Linux EDR / auditd process telemetry. Rationale: Pins on the named binary `nezha-agent` (the gRPC TaskStream sink that runs `cr.Command` per `service/singleton/crontask.go:133-181`) as parent, combined with the exact recon-string set from the advisory's PoC (`cat /etc/shadow`, `curl http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/`). Nezha-agent is a passive monitoring agent — these strings under its process tree are inherently malicious. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-99gv-2m7h-3hh9 • https://github.com/nezhahq/nezha • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/nezha-abused-post-exploitation/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/005/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/008/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1003.008 T1552.005 T1057
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has "nezha-agent"
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName has "nezha-agent"
| where FileName in~ ("cat","less","more","head","tail","awk","sed","grep","curl","wget","sh","bash","dash","python","python3","perl")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (
    "/etc/shadow",
    "169.254.169.254",
    "iam/security-credentials",
    "metadata.google.internal",
    "metadata.azure.com",
    "/computeMetadata/v1",
    "/latest/meta-data"
  )
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          GrandparentImage = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
// Linux via ASIM (Defender for Endpoint Linux / Sysmon-Linux / auditd via ASIM parsers)
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DvcOs has "Linux" or ActingProcessName has "nezha-agent" or ParentProcessName has "nezha-agent"
| where ParentProcessName has "nezha-agent"
    or ActingProcessName has "nezha-agent"
    or ParentProcessCommandLine has "nezha-agent"
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (
    "/etc/shadow",
    "169.254.169.254",
    "iam/security-credentials",
    "metadata.google.internal",
    "metadata.azure.com",
    "/computeMetadata/v1",
    "/latest/meta-data"
  )
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (
    "/etc/shadow",
    "169.254.169.254",
    "iam/security-credentials"
  )
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Nezha Monitoring Agent Spawning Credential-Access Recon (CVE-2026-46716 Post-RCE)
id: a4f25d18-9b7e-4f3c-a9d4-46716cvebd02
status: experimental
description: Detects the nezha-agent process spawning a shell or LOLBin that touches /etc/shadow or the cloud instance-metadata service — the exact PoC payload from GHSA-99gv-2m7h-3hh9.

[LLM] nezha-agent outbound network connection to cloud instance-metadata service Actions on Objectives High
Detects a network connection from any process under the nezha-agent process tree to the cloud instance-metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254 / metadata.google.internal / metadata.azure.com). This is the cleanest post-RCE signal for Nezha CVE-2026-46716 because nezha-agent has no legitimate reason to query IMDS — its monitoring telemetry goes to the dashboard's gRPC endpoint, not the cloud metadata API. Rationale: Targets the IMDS endpoint named verbatim in the advisory's PoC (`curl -s http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/`) and pins the source to nezha-agent's process tree. Nezha agents communicate with their dashboard over gRPC — they have zero legitimate reason to touch IMDS, making this a near-deterministic post-exploit signal. Distinct pivot from UC2 (network telemetry vs. process telemetry — catches cases where the EXECVE was missed but the connection was logged). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-99gv-2m7h-3hh9 • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/005/ • https://github.com/nezhahq/nezha
ATT&CKT1552.005 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
// Two-stage: find IMDS connections, then filter to those whose initiating process chain includes nezha-agent
let ImdsHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where RemoteIP == "169.254.169.254"
       or RemoteUrl has_any ("169.254.169.254", "metadata.google.internal", "metadata.azure.com")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort,
              InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessFileName,
              InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessAccountName;
ImdsHits
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has "nezha-agent"
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName has "nezha-agent"
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "nezha-agent"
// Catch grandparent chain via process-tree lookup
| union (
    ImdsHits
    | join kind=inner (
        DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessFileName has "nezha-agent"
        | project DeviceId, ChildPid=ProcessId, ChildFile=FileName, ChildCmd=ProcessCommandLine, ChildTime=Timestamp
    ) on DeviceId
    | where InitiatingProcessId == ChildPid and Timestamp between (ChildTime .. ChildTime + 10m)
  )
| order by Timestamp desc
// Network connection to IMDS where the originating process chain involves nezha-agent
let ImdsConn = ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where DstIpAddr == "169.254.169.254"
       or DstHostname has_any ("metadata.google.internal", "metadata.azure.com");
let NezhaProcs = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessName has "nezha-agent"
       or ParentProcessName has "nezha-agent"
       or ParentProcessCommandLine has "nezha-agent"
    | project DvcHostname, NezhaProcPid=TargetProcessId, NezhaTime=TimeGenerated, NezhaCmd=TargetProcessCommandLine;
ImdsConn
| join kind=inner NezhaProcs on DvcHostname
| where TimeGenerated between (NezhaTime .. NezhaTime + 10m)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber, NezhaCmd, NezhaTime
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] Endpoint visits to Russian-speaking cybercrime forums Exploit.in / XSS.is
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound connections to seized First VPN exit node IPs · [LLM] Endpoint resolution or web traffic to seized 1vpns[.]com/net/org domains · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] Outbound connections to seized First VPN exit node IPs Command & Control High
Detects internal endpoints or perimeter devices initiating connections to the three U.S.-located First VPN exit-node IPs published by the FBI flash alert (2.223.66.103, 5.181.234.59, 92.38.148.58). Hits indicate prior use of the takedown-targeted criminal VPN — either by a malicious insider, a compromised host beaconing back through the old infrastructure, or law-enforcement sinkhole traffic worth triaging. Rationale: Uses the three exact U.S. exit-node IPs (2.223.66.103, 5.181.234.59, 92.38.148.58) named in the FBI flash alert quoted in the article. Static IPs published by law enforcement post-seizure are high-fidelity IOCs with effectively zero legitimate enterprise use. Cross-checked against: • https://www.europol.europa.eu/media-press/newsroom • https://www.ic3.gov/
ATT&CKT1090.003 T1572
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
let exitNodes = dynamic(["2.223.66.103","5.181.234.59","92.38.148.58"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (exitNodes)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
let exitNodes = dynamic(["2.223.66.103","5.181.234.59","92.38.148.58"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DestinationIP in (exitNodes)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=SourceHostName, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, ApplicationProtocol, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct),
  (ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DstIpAddr in (exitNodes)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=SrcHostname, SourceIP=SrcIpAddr, DestinationIP=DstIpAddr, DestinationPort=DstPortNumber, ApplicationProtocol=NetworkApplicationProtocol, DeviceVendor=EventVendor, DeviceProduct=EventProduct)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Outbound Connection to Seized First VPN Exit Node IP

[LLM] Endpoint resolution or web traffic to seized 1vpns[.]com/net/org domains Command & Control High
Catches any internal host that resolves or browses to the three seized First VPN domains (1vpns.com / 1vpns.net / 1vpns.org). Post-takedown, any contact is either a forensic indicator of prior use, malware with stale C2/proxy config still beaconing, or an insider continuing to attempt access to the criminal service. Rationale: The three domains (1vpns.com, 1vpns.net, 1vpns.org) are quoted directly from the Eurojust seizure list in the article. Post-seizure these resolve to sinkholes or NX — any traffic from a corporate host is a confirmed historical-use signal worth alerting on. Cross-checked against: • https://www.eurojust.europa.eu/news • https://www.europol.europa.eu/media-press/newsroom
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1090.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
let domains = dynamic(["1vpns.com","1vpns.net","1vpns.org"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (domains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
let domains = dynamic(["1vpns.com","1vpns.net","1vpns.org"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Name has_any (domains)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, ClientIP, Domain=Name, QueryType=QueryTypeName, Answer=tostring(Result)),
  (ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DnsQuery has_any (domains)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Domain=DnsQuery, QueryType=DnsQueryTypeName, Answer=DnsResponseName),
  (ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where HttpHostName has_any (domains) or Url has_any (domains)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Domain=HttpHostName, QueryType="HTTP", Answer=Url)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: DNS Query for Seized First VPN Domains (1vpns.com/net/org)

[LLM] Endpoint visits to Russian-speaking cybercrime forums Exploit.in / XSS.is Reconnaissance Medium
Detects internal hosts resolving or browsing to exploit.in and xss.is — the two Russian-speaking cybercrime forums named in the article as the marketing channels for First VPN. Used to surface insider threats, employees moonlighting in cybercrime, or compromised hosts being driven to acquire offensive tooling. Rationale: Both forums (exploit.in, xss.is) are named verbatim in the article as the Russian-speaking criminal marketplaces where First VPN was advertised. They have no legitimate corporate business purpose; access from a production endpoint is high-signal insider/compromise telemetry. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1588/002/ • https://www.recordedfuture.com/research
ATT&CKT1593.002 T1588.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
let forums = dynamic(["exploit.in","xss.is"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (forums)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let forums = dynamic(["exploit.in","xss.is"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Name has_any (forums)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, ClientIP, Domain=Name, Url="", UserAgent=""),
  (ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where HttpHostName has_any (forums) or Url has_any (forums)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Domain=HttpHostName, Url, UserAgent=HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent),
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DestinationHostName has_any (forums) or RequestURL has_any (forums)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=SourceHostName, ClientIP=SourceIP, Domain=DestinationHostName, Url=RequestURL, UserAgent=RequestClientApplication)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

description: Detects DNS resolution for exploit.in and xss.is, the two cybercrime forums named in the May 2026 First VPN takedown reporting as marketing channels for criminal infrastructure.

  condition: selection
falsepositives:

(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:22 @QueryName:(*exploit.in OR *xss.is)) OR (source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationHostname:(*exploit.in OR *xss.is)) OR (source:linux.syslog ("exploit.in" OR "xss.is"))
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(^|\.)(exploit\.in|xss\.is)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())
